name: Rosace
author: E. T. Carter
description: A rose-engine guilloché: two families of concentric rosette curves, their petal lobes precessing with radius into a spirograph weave, engraved as fine bright hairlines into a dark burnished-metal ground. Where the families cross they interleave into the dense barleycorn moiré guilloché is prized for, the crests catching a rolling specular glint. The whole rose turns slowly on its lathe while the lobe phases drift, so the engraving shimmers and breathes without ever freezing — the engine still cutting.

params.label: Petals
params.effect: Number of lobes per rosette ring — low gives a broad scalloped rose, high a fine many-pointed star.

params.label: Line density
params.effect: How many concentric engraved lines cross the medallion — low reads as bold grooves, high as a fine hairline weave.

params.label: Lobe depth
params.effect: Depth of the petal modulation — 0 gives plain concentric rings, 1 swings the lobes into deep spirograph waves.

params.label: Lathe speed
params.effect: Rate the rose turns and its lobe phases drift — how fast the engine-turned shimmer rolls across the engraving.
